# Proto-Reptile
Albeit not as popular as in the rest of the galaxy, the protogen movement reached even the Unathi who viewed it as a great tool to strengthen their bodies, thus proto-Unathi are quite common to see.
## Racial Features - They [color=#ffa500]cannot eat vegetables[/color], but [color=#1e90ff]can eat raw meat and drink blood without any ill effects[/color]. - Their blood has a dark red color. - Due to being cold blooded. They take [color=#ffa500]20% more Cold damage[/color] and [color=#1fb0ff]50% less heat damage[/color]. - Thanks to their plating and scales they take [color=#1fb0ff]10% less slash damage[/color]. - On top of that, they receive [color=#1fb0ff](10%-30%-40%) slash and piercing damage resistance[/color] depending on their cybernetic choice. (Access your species specific loadout from the Appearance tab) - They have a [color=#1fb0ff]Built in MIDI player[/color] - Due to their mixed mechanical and biological nature, they can [color=#1fb0ff]heal with both chemicals and topicals, and welders and wires[/color], however [color=#ffa500]both methods are only 50% effective[/color]. - They are [color=#ffa500]damaged slightly and immobilised by EMPs[/color]. - They have an in-built [color=#1fb0ff]Trinary Radio Channel accessed with the key :D[/color] - They can drag objects with their tail, keeping both their hands free. - Thanks to their claws, they deal [color=red]5[/color] slash damage with unarmed attacks. - Their standard body heat is 37 degrees Celcius and they [color=#1e90ff]can withstand temperatures between 12 and 130 degrees Celcius[/color].
## Draconic and Trinary The Unathi language, known as Draconic, is composed of a series of sibilant hisses and rattles. Despite its harsh sounds, it is actually one of the easiest languages for other species to learn due to only requiring a tongue to reproduce the sounds necessary. Like all other Protogens, they are also able to speak and understand Trinary, a language similar to binary but able to be spoken by most synthetics.
## Age and Names Unathi are a long lives species, reaching adulthood at 18 years of age and being capable of living up to 200 years. Their names are given to them during the early stages of their life, usually describing one of the typical actions of the hatchling. Most commonly, Unathi names follow the format "(Verb)-the-(Noun)" but it is not uncommon to see names that stray from this pattern.
